    - Not entitled to dividends
    - can be freely bought and sold to facilitate game play
    - has a 1 token to 0.001 vote voting weightage

Figured out Forking as the way for DAO community to accomodate projects by fulfilling these needs: 

- irreconcilable and conflicting market thesis and management styles. 
- Apart from alleviating conflicts, it serves the purposes of reducing churn amongst actively contributing volunteers in our DAO community
- Forking ensures all prior contributors' efforts are ackowledged and equitably accounted in such situations
- creates more surface area for more volunteers to support DAO mission and purpose to fight "Fake News"
- reduce communication overhead and excessive efforts in aligning ever growing number of contributions in a project
- spreads DAO risk over multiple projects as opposed to consolidating all eggs in one basket (project)
- allow DAO to remain decentralized while still enjoying the benefit of a strong core leadership for each project

Soft forked project 
- Allows a parent project to "theorectically" sponsor a child project. 
- Contributions to a child project is still recorded on the parent project's ledger but labelled differently
- Contributions to the child project are still awarded governance tokens of the parent project
- Revenue generated by child project are held in the parent project vault

Hard forked project 
- Child project has claim independence of parent project
- Contributions to a child project is recorded on its own branced off version of the paren project's ledger
- Contributions to the child project are awarded governacen tokens in the child project.
- Revenue generated by child project are held in its own project vault

30 minutes face time to chat about the contextual framing of the conversations in the beer hall channel

The value of Beer Hall

- a place to surface unknown unknowns via discussion. A lot of the topics surfaced here ends up becoming trends that inform what potential projects to pursue next

- a place where members of the DAO can come together to get to interact with each other in a generally informal setting

-  a place where useful information about DAO operations can be surfaced, discussed upon and eventually voted upon

- a place where members can have visibility into the kind of value that is exchange hands between various DAO members. In other spaces, a lot of these kind of exchanges are done in privacy so other members who might be able to jump in to participate ends up missing out because they don't know the deal flow is happening. In fact most of the introductions I made, they are done here in this channel except those that have some NDA concerns in place.

*Proposed governance token management protocol*

The purpose of this protocol is to discourage excessive speculation on our governance tokens in the open market once it gets listed on Centralized exchanges while at the same time capitalize on market fluctuations to increased our fiat netbook value per issued governance token ratio



*_Rules_*
    - _*Rule 1*_: every quarter DAO will make provisions to increase governance tokens in circulation by 25% of what is already in circulation last day of the previous quarter. 

    - _*Rule 2*_: Full amount might not end up being circulated in the market if no exceptional price ranges present themselves 

    - _*Rule 3*_: DAO will make open market purchase as and when market value at which governance token is traded at falls below USDT net book value. 

    - _*Rule 4*_: DAO will make open market sales of governance tokens up to the total provision specified for market circulation as and when market value per token exceeds the minimal of either USDT1 or USDT net book value per token



*_Conclusion_* 
This protocol for governance token management when strictly adhered to in the long haul is anti-dilutive on nature. 

It has the effect of discouraging excessive speculation activities beyond desirable price range both on the upside and the downside 

The muting of speculative components in open market pricing of DAO governance token help curtail distractions DAO governance token holders might otherwise experience away from daily practice of Satseva

    _Rule 1_ - full amount of first initial sale in USD from buyer brought in by DAO, same exact amount is issued to DAO member who helped made the sale in TDG

I think this approach of directly serving samples of cacao to every single vendor at their booth suggested by Atelier is more well suited for such kinds of gatherings if the intention is to acquire vendors 

Might end up being more scalable than holding cacao circles directly targeting consumers since most consumers as observed is usually a one off hence the CAC (_customer acquisition cost_) versus the LTV (_customer life time value_) is not as positive on the _Return on Capital_ deployed 

To optimize the model, you want to drive down *_CAC*_ as much as possible and target demographics with the highest possible *_LTV X Conversion rates*_ multiple 

ideally if possible drive CAC down to Zero, hence why I have been spending time doing all the trash run to get pass the gates free of charge and systematically utilizing food banks to cut down food related operating expenses

[CONTRIBUTION EVENT]
- Type: Time (Minutes)
- Amount: 240
- Description: Agroverse Shop Updates
  
  Updates to the Agroverse shop:
  
  NEW EXPERIENCES ADDED
  Added two seasonal experiences to the Pacific West Coast journey where cacao is offered:
  
  • Slab City & Salvation Mountain - The Last Free Place in America
    https://agroverse.shop/cacao-journeys/pacific-west-coast-path/experiences/slab-city-salvation-mountain/index.html
  
  • Winter Desert Gatherings - Quartzite, Salton Sea & Joshua Tree
    https://agroverse.shop/cacao-journeys/pacific-west-coast-path/experiences/winter-desert-gatherings/index.html
  
  These gatherings (Tribe Boheme, Van Aid, SchooliePalooza, Bombay Beach Binnelie, Boondockers bash, Quartzite gem show, Rubber Tramp Rendezvous) occur during winter season (Thanksgiving through end of winter) and are now part of the journey map.
  
  TASTE PROFILE VISUALIZATIONS
  Added interactive taste profile charts to shipment pages. The inclusion of these taste graphs was inspired by noticing them on one of the cacao brands that Kirsten shared. Process:
  
  1. Took photos of taste profile sheets from CIC (Cacao Innovation Center)
  2. Used Grok to generate a detailed prompt
  3. Used that prompt with Cursor AI to generate the code
  4. Embedded interactive D3.js charts on each shipment page
  
  Taste profiles available on:
  https://agroverse.shop/shipments/agl4/index.html
  https://agroverse.shop/shipments/agl6/index.html
  https://agroverse.shop/shipments/agl8/index.html
  
  COMMUNITY COLLABORATION
  Discussed taste profiling with Matheus. Since taste is subjective, we don't need to pay CIC for this. We have a community of chocolate makers and chocolatiers in San Francisco who can be involved in the process, making it more authentic and community-driven.
  
  THOUGHTS ON AI & WEB EVOLUTION
  Observations on web evolution:
  
  • Web 1.0 (Geocities era) - Rich, handcrafted pages, complex ecosystem
  • Web 1.5 (MySpace) - Mix of handcrafted and templated
  • Web 2.0 (Facebook) - Everything templatized for scale
  • Web 3.0 (AI era) - AI could handcraft pages, bringing back Web 1.0 richness without the heavy human lifting... the only question is a site fully ran based on this paradigm can it be scalable
  
  Experimenting with AI as a creative partner to build unique, handcrafted experiences at scale. The taste profile charts are an example - each tailored to the specific shipment without manually coding every one.

[CONTRIBUTION EVENT]
- Type: Time (Minutes)
- Amount: 120
- Description: Got this repository up and running so that future LLMs on other machines can easily come up to speed on context to handle various tasks within our DAO ecoystem
  
  https://github.com/TrueSightDAO/agentic_ai_context
  
  Basically human getting AIs to teach AIs so that humans dont need to teach again
  
  Started experimenting with the following come online based LLMs as opposed to cursor AI for eventual deployment to the cloud
  
  - Gemini CLI
  - ⁠Grok CLI
  - ⁠Claude CLI
  - ⁠Codex CLI
  
  Spent some time thinking through the architecture of how other RAG (_Retreival Augmentation Generation_) infrastructure have been set up 
  
  My sense is instead of incurring a bunch of server cost setting up a vector space database which we don’t really need at our scale as well as the simplicity of what we are doing 
  
  Pre-compile all our DAO’s knowledge based data as vectors and index them as flat files. 
  
  When we need the LLM to make specialized decisions within our context, just have one of the servers convert a query that is being passed in by the user into a vector and do a Euclidean comparison of the query versus all the other factors in the index files to retrieve the right contacts and then pass them to LLM we are utilizing to get the final result to return to the user.
  
  And if the data size becomes a little larger, we just shove the pre-compound vectors into an SQL light database, which is due a flat file that can be easily ported from one server to another. 
  
  Recurring modes of usage that I can think of 
  
  - on boarding of new prospective members
  - ⁠ existing members who wants to get caught up on what has happened in the DAO recently
  - ⁠ freight and shipping configurations
  - ⁠ production cost optimization configurations
  - ⁠ go to market and store outreach strategy
  - ⁠ stores re-stocking strategy
  - ⁠ social media content, marketing ongoing efforts and strategy
  
  My sense is once the stack is implemented. I got to spend less time on all this stuff that requires a lot of logic and just kinda mechanical and perhaps repetitive. 
  
  Instead spend more time on face-to-face interactions for business development and trust building purposes.

- Governance token

    - can be converted to utility tokens

    - has a 1 token to 1 vote voting weightage

    - Not entitled to dividends
    - can be freely bought and sold to facilitate game play
    - has a 1 token to 0.001 vote voting weightage

raw_contributions.Contribution Made:
Figured out Forking as the way for DAO community to accomodate projects by fulfilling these needs: 

- irreconcilable and conflicting market thesis and management styles. 
- Apart from alleviating conflicts, it serves the purposes of reducing churn amongst actively contributing volunteers in our DAO community
- Forking ensures all prior contributors' efforts are ackowledged and equitably accounted in such situations
- creates more surface area for more volunteers to support DAO mission and purpose to fight "Fake News"
- reduce communication overhead and excessive efforts in aligning ever growing number of contributions in a project
- spreads DAO risk over multiple projects as opposed to consolidating all eggs in one basket (project)
- allow DAO to remain decentralized while still enjoying the benefit of a strong core leadership for each project

Soft forked project 
- Allows a parent project to "theorectically" sponsor a child project. 
- Contributions to a child project is still recorded on the parent project's ledger but labelled differently
- Contributions to the child project are still awarded governance tokens of the parent project
- Revenue generated by child project are held in the parent project vault

Hard forked project 
- Child project has claim independence of parent project
- Contributions to a child project is recorded on its own branced off version of the paren project's ledger
- Contributions to the child project are awarded governacen tokens in the child project.
- Revenue generated by child project are held in its own project vault

raw_contributions.Contribution Made:
The value of Beer Hall

- a place to surface unknown unknowns via discussion. A lot of the topics surfaced here ends up becoming trends that inform what potential projects to pursue next

- a place where members of the DAO can come together to get to interact with each other in a generally informal setting

-  a place where useful information about DAO operations can be surfaced, discussed upon and eventually voted upon

- a place where members can have visibility into the kind of value that is exchange hands between various DAO members. In other spaces, a lot of these kind of exchanges are done in privacy so other members who might be able to jump in to participate ends up missing out because they don't know the deal flow is happening. In fact most of the introductions I made, they are done here in this channel except those that have some NDA concerns in place.

*Proposed governance token management protocol*

The purpose of this protocol is to discourage excessive speculation on our governance tokens in the open market once it gets listed on Centralized exchanges while at the same time capitalize on market fluctuations to increased our fiat netbook value per issued governance token ratio



*_Rules_*
    - _*Rule 1*_: every quarter DAO will make provisions to increase governance tokens in circulation by 25% of what is already in circulation last day of the previous quarter. 

    - _*Rule 2*_: Full amount might not end up being circulated in the market if no exceptional price ranges present themselves 

    - _*Rule 3*_: DAO will make open market purchase as and when market value at which governance token is traded at falls below USDT net book value. 

    - _*Rule 4*_: DAO will make open market sales of governance tokens up to the total provision specified for market circulation as and when market value per token exceeds the minimal of either USDT1 or USDT net book value per token



*_Conclusion_* 
This protocol for governance token management when strictly adhered to in the long haul is anti-dilutive on nature. 

It has the effect of discouraging excessive speculation activities beyond desirable price range both on the upside and the downside 

The muting of speculative components in open market pricing of DAO governance token help curtail distractions DAO governance token holders might otherwise experience away from daily practice of Satseva

My thoughts regarding all these recent discussions about commission from sales of cacao nibs…

Here is a good analogy… 

All these chefs in the kitchen are spending alot of cycles debating on the size of the shovel the gardeners working on the farm in the backyard should be using 

Meanwhile none of the chefs in the kitchen have  ever the intent of actually rolling up their sleeves to dig a hole in the farm using the shovel or have ever done so.

After observing the above described episode and then observing how things were done in the Zen monastery as well as recalling how logistics in the Singapore military was ran during my 2.5 years there see below. 

*Key takeaways*
- saying don’t do this or that, but not stating clearly what exactly needs to be done is not helpful. Except for the purpose of entertainment during free time, it almost definitely a waste of time reading the text

- ⁠surface rules that are objective, measurable and positive 

- ⁠surface actual rules that could be compiled together to define a recipe/protocol/policy that could be executed step by step, tested and then fine tuned

- ⁠person surfacing rules for compilation into recipe/protocol/policy should be one who have actually rolled up sleeves and dug a hole or is about to start digging a hole with a shovel. definitely not by folks who are solely intent on just hanging around in the kitchen speculating what size of hole that is to be dug on the farm and what size shovel 

- ⁠for everyone to feel included, once the gardeners have surfaced the recipe/protocol/policy for voting, everyone feel free to cast your vote 

- ⁠when someone surfaces a rule, critically access the signal from the noise. 

- ⁠signal: from person who is truly intent on digging the hole or has already dug one. 

- ⁠noise: from person who is just speculating and has no intention of doing so

*Examples of what are rules and what are not*

_Valid proposed rule_
- for each additional 1 centimeters of width in a hole, the depth needs to be increased by 2 centimeters. 
- ⁠For holes deeper than 10 centimeters, please use large shovel. 
- ⁠For holes lesser than 10 centimeters, please use small shovel. 


_Invalid proposed rules_
- the hole needs to be big. (_what do you mean by big_)

@16468233438 I relooked into our costing of our most recent shipment from Brazil into USA

*Cost of the goods itself*
- 100KG cacao nibs: $R6500 = USD1,310.3846

*Cost of the transportation and customs* 
- _Leitl Express_ - Trucking from Ilheus to Salvador: $R1066.85 = USD215.11019
- _Omega Services_ - Air Freight from Salvador to SF Airport: $R4000 = USD806.53795
- _SeaCoast Logistics_ - Custom Clearance at SF Airport: USD561.03

If our goal is to bring cost per KG down to USD20 and still pay the farmers the fair price they are asking for than shipping and freighting cost needs to go down. 

Four options to optimize our supply chain bound for USA
- ⁠Find cheaper freight forwarding company
- ⁠Do sea freight instead of air freight
- Increase shipping volume to acquire economies of scale. _but first we need to decipher which cost is fixed and which cost is variable_
- ⁠Figure out how to do customs clearance ourselves to save on the USD561.03 by removing SeaCoast Logistics from the equation. _Doesn’t feel like Grazie is actually doing much for us but still charging us stuff_.

*Proposal to SF LUV from Agroverse*

*Date:* March 5, 2025  

Dear SF LUV Team,  

We are excited to introduce Agroverse, a project operated by TrueSight DAO, dedicated to regenerating 10,000 hectares of Amazon rainforest. Our mission is to support cacao farmers who practice agroforestry, helping them regrow the rainforest on formerly deforested land in the Amazonian region. By purchasing premium regenerative cacao directly from these farmers, we distribute it to conscious consumers in the USA and Europe, fostering sustainable agriculture, environmental restoration, and economic empowerment for local communities.  

We are reaching out to explore a potential collaboration with SF LUV as a merchant partner. Given our shared commitment to positive impact, we believe Agroverse’s regenerative cacao aligns well with your values. We are currently distributing in San Francisco and would love to offer your community the opportunity to purchase our cacao using the SF LUV token.  

To make this partnership seamless, we’d like to understand how we can redeem SF LUV tokens for cash after accepting them as payment for our cacao. Could you please provide details on the redemption process, including any requirements or steps involved? We’re eager to integrate this innovative payment option and deepen our impact in the San Francisco market.  

We look forward to hearing from you and exploring how we can work together to create a meaningful partnership. Please feel free to contact us at [insert contact info] for further discussion.  

Warm regards,  
Gary  
A Contributor

The first thing that came to mind this morning when I woke up and thought through all the signals gathered from the ecosystem and beyond so far is that we might have already achieved *_product market fit*_

Me and @⁨Kirsten Ritschel⁩ spent 30 minutes two evenings ago discussing about holding cacao circles here in the Bay Area while I am away. She commenting that the product is pretty much selling itself at this point 

Jerry mentioned three months ago when we were discussing the qualitative data gathered from our growth hack into local stores that it is a very very healthy sign that the sales cycle is extremely short (_in a matter of few minutes_) after presenting the call to action to venue operators who are value aligned versus infinitely long (_zero conversion_) when speaking to venue operators who are not-values aligned 

The cacao was invited into the two exclusive climate week gatherings where values aligned individuals were gathered 

From my perspective, product market fit is like deciphering if the economy is now in recession, it only becomes apparent in hindsight once you have crossed the threshold 

From a high level perspective the following is clear

- *WHY*: Regenerate our Amazon rainforest because it is important for the continued survival of our species on earth 

- ⁠*WHAT*: Bags of cacao sourced from farmers actively restoring it 

- ⁠*HOW*: still in the crowd sourced experimentation phase. And this is the current phase of where our meta-game


https://mailchimp.com/resources/product-market-fit/#:~:text=%22Product%2Dmarket%20fit%2C%22,%2C%20that's%20product%2Dmarket%20fit.

Me and @kikiscocoa spent an hour in a facetime session. Items and schedules for this year discussed 

- Summer time is a challenging time to ship chocolate as it melts.

- ⁠The state the packages arrives in San Francisco is not acceptable if we are going to ship direct to our consignees, USPS doesn't treat the cacao with the reverence that it should have. We need to improve the way we pack the cacao before it ships out of @⁨Matheus Reis - Bahia Coop⁩ warehouse in Ilheus to safeguard against that

- ⁠Exclusive cacao circles in San Francisco targeted specifically at chocolatiers in Bay Area to showcase what we have available in our warehouse. Each of this exclusive cacao circle will be restricted to just 6 participants for a cosy intimate setting much like the cacao circle we had at the Festivals up here where we got to connect with other vendors present

- ⁠The *Radical Transparency* we introduced into our supply chain is something that resonates with chocolatiers

- Chocolatiers ⁠always face the constant challenge where suppliers abandon their cacao because something else more lucrative come about

- The sales lead list gathered from San Francisco Chocolatier festival will be a great way to feed participants into our summer time exclusive cacao circles. 

- ⁠Summer time in the North is also the time to be in the Southern hemisphere as it is cacao harvesting season.

I spent 1.5 hour brewing the ice cold cacao and walking the faire grounds to offer it to vendors 

I think this approach of directly serving samples of cacao to every single vendor at their booth suggested by Atelier is more well suited for such kinds of gatherings if the intention is to acquire vendors 

Might end up being more scalable than holding cacao circles directly targeting consumers since most consumers as observed is usually a one off hence the CAC (_customer acquisition cost_) versus the LTV (_customer life time value_) is not as positive on the _Return on Capital_ deployed 

To optimize the model, you want to drive down *_CAC*_ as much as possible and target demographics with the highest possible *_LTV X Conversion rates*_ multiple 

ideally if possible drive CAC down to Zero, hence why I have been spending time doing all the trash run to get pass the gates free of charge and systematically utilizing food banks to cut down food related operating expenses

raw_contributions.Contribution Made:
[CONTRIBUTION EVENT]
- Type: Time (Minutes)
- Amount: 240
- Description: Agroverse Shop Updates
  
  Updates to the Agroverse shop:
  
  NEW EXPERIENCES ADDED
  Added two seasonal experiences to the Pacific West Coast journey where cacao is offered:
  
  • Slab City & Salvation Mountain - The Last Free Place in America
    https://agroverse.shop/cacao-journeys/pacific-west-coast-path/experiences/slab-city-salvation-mountain/index.html
  
  • Winter Desert Gatherings - Quartzite, Salton Sea & Joshua Tree
    https://agroverse.shop/cacao-journeys/pacific-west-coast-path/experiences/winter-desert-gatherings/index.html
  
  These gatherings (Tribe Boheme, Van Aid, SchooliePalooza, Bombay Beach Binnelie, Boondockers bash, Quartzite gem show, Rubber Tramp Rendezvous) occur during winter season (Thanksgiving through end of winter) and are now part of the journey map.
  
  TASTE PROFILE VISUALIZATIONS
  Added interactive taste profile charts to shipment pages. The inclusion of these taste graphs was inspired by noticing them on one of the cacao brands that Kirsten shared. Process:
  
  1. Took photos of taste profile sheets from CIC (Cacao Innovation Center)
  2. Used Grok to generate a detailed prompt
  3. Used that prompt with Cursor AI to generate the code
  4. Embedded interactive D3.js charts on each shipment page
  
  Taste profiles available on:
  https://agroverse.shop/shipments/agl4/index.html
  https://agroverse.shop/shipments/agl6/index.html
  https://agroverse.shop/shipments/agl8/index.html
  
  COMMUNITY COLLABORATION
  Discussed taste profiling with Matheus. Since taste is subjective, we don't need to pay CIC for this. We have a community of chocolate makers and chocolatiers in San Francisco who can be involved in the process, making it more authentic and community-driven.
  
  THOUGHTS ON AI & WEB EVOLUTION
  Observations on web evolution:
  
  • Web 1.0 (Geocities era) - Rich, handcrafted pages, complex ecosystem
  • Web 1.5 (MySpace) - Mix of handcrafted and templated
  • Web 2.0 (Facebook) - Everything templatized for scale
  • Web 3.0 (AI era) - AI could handcraft pages, bringing back Web 1.0 richness without the heavy human lifting... the only question is a site fully ran based on this paradigm can it be scalable
  
  Experimenting with AI as a creative partner to build unique, handcrafted experiences at scale. The taste profile charts are an example - each tailored to the specific shipment without manually coding every one.

raw_contributions.Contribution Made:
[CONTRIBUTION EVENT]
- Type: Time (Minutes)
- Amount: 120
- Description: Got this repository up and running so that future LLMs on other machines can easily come up to speed on context to handle various tasks within our DAO ecoystem
  
  https://github.com/TrueSightDAO/agentic_ai_context
  
  Basically human getting AIs to teach AIs so that humans dont need to teach again
  
  Started experimenting with the following come online based LLMs as opposed to cursor AI for eventual deployment to the cloud
  
  - Gemini CLI
  - ⁠Grok CLI
  - ⁠Claude CLI
  - ⁠Codex CLI
  
  Spent some time thinking through the architecture of how other RAG (_Retreival Augmentation Generation_) infrastructure have been set up 
  
  My sense is instead of incurring a bunch of server cost setting up a vector space database which we don’t really need at our scale as well as the simplicity of what we are doing 
  
  Pre-compile all our DAO’s knowledge based data as vectors and index them as flat files. 
  
  When we need the LLM to make specialized decisions within our context, just have one of the servers convert a query that is being passed in by the user into a vector and do a Euclidean comparison of the query versus all the other factors in the index files to retrieve the right contacts and then pass them to LLM we are utilizing to get the final result to return to the user.
  
  And if the data size becomes a little larger, we just shove the pre-compound vectors into an SQL light database, which is due a flat file that can be easily ported from one server to another. 
  
  Recurring modes of usage that I can think of 
  
  - on boarding of new prospective members
  - ⁠ existing members who wants to get caught up on what has happened in the DAO recently
  - ⁠ freight and shipping configurations
  - ⁠ production cost optimization configurations
  - ⁠ go to market and store outreach strategy
  - ⁠ stores re-stocking strategy
  - ⁠ social media content, marketing ongoing efforts and strategy
  
  My sense is once the stack is implemented. I got to spend less time on all this stuff that requires a lot of logic and just kinda mechanical and perhaps repetitive. 
  
  Instead spend more time on face-to-face interactions for business development and trust building purposes.

  ## What changed
  
  Diagnosed and fixed three production bugs on `perch.truesight.me` (sentiment_importer):
  
  ### 1. Landing page 500: Date.parse on Time object (sentiment_importer#1097)
  - `get_date_range_for_market` in `app/helpers/application_helper.rb` called `Date.parse()` on raw PostgreSQL results, but PG returns `date_published` as a `Time` object, not a `String`. This caused `TypeError: no implicit conversion of Time into String` on every request to `/`.
  - Fix: Changed `Date.parse(r['date_published'])` to `r['date_published'].to_date`.
  
  ### 2. /large_dips 500: broken route helper shadowing (sentiment_importer#1098)
  - Commit 08c42e24 introduced `helper_method :my_shopping_path` and `helper_method :large_dips_path` in `daily_trades_controller.rb` that called non-existent `my_shopping_daily_trades_path` and `large_dips_daily_trades_path` route helpers, shadowing the valid route-generated helper.
  - Fix: Removed both helper methods so the route helpers resolve correctly.
  
  ### 3. Charts missing data after June 11, 2026 (sentiment_importer#1099)
  - `LargeDipIndexRefresher` (app/workers/large_dip_index_refresher.rb) referenced `MINIMUM_TRADE_COUNT` without the `DailyTrade::` qualifier, causing `NameError` on every run since June 11. Raw price data imported fine, but sell-off index records (used by the charts) were never created.
  - Fix: Changed `MINIMUM_TRADE_COUNT` to `DailyTrade::MINIMUM_TRADE_COUNT`. Backfilled 13 missing June trading days.
  
  ### Infrastructure fixes during deployment
  - `seni_ror`: Killed stale `nohup` Rails process holding port 3002 with old code; cleared stale PID file blocking systemd restart.

  ## What changed

  - **Gemini integration removed** — deprecated library, non-functional API key; Grok handles all vision
  - **BigModel (ZhipuAI/GLM-4.5) LLM provider** — new provider with automatic DeepSeek fallback; ~20x cheaper than DeepSeek
  - **Deploy script key parity check** — aborts deployment if production-only `.env` keys would be lost
  
  ### DApp Governor Chat UX (dapp)
  - **Session restore re-renders proposal cards** (#210) — interactive Approve/Ignore/Reject cards recreated when reloading chat sessions
  - **All pending proposals tracked** (#210) — non-QR proposals now appear in sidebar, not just QR-coded ones
  - **Always-visible pending badge** (#210) — pending approval indicator visible without opening sidebar
  - **removePendingProposal title fallback** (#211) — non-QR proposals can be resolved from pending list
  - **Global regex for multi-block parsing** (#211) — captures all proposal JSON blocks in restored messages
  - **routes.js localhost probe fix** (#213) — prevents infinite reload loop on localhost
  
  ### Documentation (agentic_ai_context)
  - **Local debugging workflow** — authentication, DRY_RUN, golden rule (never bypass autopilot)
  - **QA testing workflow** — Playwright templates, common checks, example test
  - **Production deployment guide** — `.env` key parity, deploy/verify commands

  Autopilot can now autonomously process batches of cacao bag QR code photos end-to-end:
  1. List files in a directory
  2. Convert HEIC to JPEG
  3. Scan with pyzbar → Grok vision fallback
  4. Look up codes in DAO ledger
  
  Governor chat approval UX was broken: prior approvals weren't accessible on reload, new approvals were invisible in the sidebar. All three issues fixed and QA verified with Playwright.
  
  BigModel reduces LLM costs ~20x with automatic DeepSeek fallback for reliability.

entries.contribution: How beautiful @14153000019 🙏🏼 what a blessing. Makes me deeply happy

This is a framework that I forgot to mention that just came to mind that I used as a lens through which to think about DAO models during the early days 

the concept is described  in the book *_finite and infinite games*_ which I found sitting on a table one day 

The equivalent of finite games in our ecosystem from my perspective are the various initiatives like @⁨<guild>[initiative] Agroverse⁩ @⁨<guild>[initiative] SunMint Guild⁩ and @⁨Edgar  ⁩ 

From my perspective these are transient, their continued existence without our ecosystem is highly dependent on participants continued willingness to play them.  

The infinite game within the context of our DAO are the current rules we have in place for the tokenization of DAO member contributions. 

The rules as they are now are simple and generic enough for people to understand but at the same time flexible enough to allow participants the space to discover the finite games they want to play amongst themselves within the scope of this infinite game (_or what we refer to as the *Meta Game* in our White Paper_)

When me and @⁨Tomas - Offchain⁩ first sat down together three years ago in Buenos Aires to further explore game dynamics, the ecosystem was not yet matured enough to such an extend the finite games are aggregating real world assets to such an extend the in-game tokens of our infinite games had any material value. Back then no one really cared about the infinite game that some active participants were playing in their own heads. 

Fast forward to the present day, our in-game tokens now have actual monetary value associated with it. 

And it seems more and more external observers are awakening to the value of such infinite games and are seeking to replicate these into their own industrial verticals

An interesting idea surface within this book is how *_Evil is defined*_ 

Evil within the context of this book is defined as deliberately restricting another player’s ability to engage in the infinite game. 

From my perspective, this is where our DAO’s model start drastically differing from other DAO models out there 

bulk of existing DAO models out there are primarily centered around requiring proposals to pass via voting before associated actions are allowed, which is by design very constraining

There is very little voting events within our DAO’s model, the generic and flexible rules of our infinite game are generally permissible of any action DAO members can possibly conceive of when attempting to contribute.  

Structurally our model is more like a fly wheel which will keep just rotating so long as even a single member makes a contribution of any form. 

So the *_concept of Evil*_ as defined in the book is by design constrained from taking roots within the DAO ecosystem. And any attempt to introduce this conception of *Evil* into the ecosystem will just be met with frustration. 🤔🤣

*Problem statement 1*

Some random thoughts after attending the Natural Produce Expo to finally study end to end how conventional food distribution system works 

- large scale mono culture Farming
- ⁠aggregator 
- ⁠exporter
- ⁠freighter 
- ⁠importer 
- ⁠distributor 
- ⁠retailer 
- ⁠customers 

Right now everything from farming all the way to retailing end points seems geared for large scale operations. 

Because of this gearing, at all stages of the food distribution network as well as for the new food products productions themselves, we are forced by design to geared to require initial deployment of large volumes of capital to achieve economies of scale at some point 

- the world produces enough food to feed everybody 

- ⁠distribution is the problem 

- ⁠to achieve economies of scale trade offs are forced into the system

- current distribution system is geared for large volume of generic food products 

- ⁠ large scale single genotype monoculture is a by product of this economies of scale 

- ⁠monoculture production results in single genotype and makes supply chain vulnerable to diseases out break 

- ⁠large scale and centralized food distribution results in need for large volume of capital to be able to manufacture large quantities to push any new product through the traditional highly centralized distribution network where there are only a few gate keepers

- ⁠requirements for large capital results in need for external funding sources like those from Wall Street
 
- ⁠because distribution is large volume across large distance a lot of none-biodegradable materials are used in the package process 

- ⁠Wall Street funding forces companies to focus of share holder returns and ever increasing profit margins which means substituting Whole Foods for cheaper and less nutrient rich food ingredients 

- ⁠large scale production of volume means need to rent large commercial warehousing and storage spaces 

The really interesting question to ask is would it be possible to figure out an alternate model for food production and distribution that turns all these assumptions on its head, thereby negating the need for economies of scale, huge volumes of capital, centralized control, large scale mono-culture, utilization of large volumes of non-biodegradable packaging materials while at the same time still fulfilling the caloric and nutrient requirements of the entire human race??

- small volume
- ⁠decentralized 
- ⁠minimal packaging 
- ⁠huge diversity in food genotype within the agriculture 

I wonder if instances of such a model has priorly existed though operating on a smaller scale 

New technologies and paradigms we now have available that didn’t exist when these monolithic food product and distribution systems came about

- worldwide instantaneous communication and proliferation of knowledge via the Internet 

- ⁠3D printing for small batch production 

- ⁠blockchain and cryptocurrencies to align incentives across distributed communities of people 

- ⁠robotics and AI are on the way to making human involvement redundant in the production of food 

- ⁠people are ok with AirBnb, hence ok with having access to facility without necessary the need for ownership

Feels like one of those very meaty and interesting engineering problems to hack on 🤩🙏

https://app.realms.today/dao/2yH36PrWii3RthpHtdJVYaPgBzfcSLe7oevvGRavrut7/proposal/BuPC3Ufen6PCyXvgoYuFx498ut99a7W4ZFDeHmcwtRDq

- Current Formula: Maximum of (1 - price of our $TDG token, 1 month USA Treasury Yield )
- New Formula: Minimum of (price of our $TDG token, 1)

Reasons:

1. Bulk of DAO members are token holders and don’t really trade on the tokens. People actively selling their tokens are residents of developing countries seeking to make a livelihood through the active contributions instead of holding it for speculation purposes. 

2. When they sell the tokens, the price will fall and gas fee should fall to reflect the change in stake, this encourages more people to utilize the network for transacting cacao for their own needs

3. When revenue by the network increases, token prices will increase, encouraging people living in developing countries who need to cash out to cash out 

4. When price of token goes above one and none of the existing token holders are cashing, then DAO can do an open market sale of tokens to bring it back within range thereby increasing available resources in our vault to conduct on our asset transactions

5. Finally this new formula is easier to explain compared to the old one which becomes a mouthful after a while
